evidence.title: New sign-ins bounce
evidence.body: 31% of new sign-ins fail the certificate check. Sessions that already exist are untouched.

evidence.title: Sessions signed by ca-18
evidence.body: Every rejected sign-in carries a chain issued by ca-18, promoted at 01:12 without a change ticket. 31,240 sessions have been signed by it in the last 40 minutes.

evidence.title: Issuer ahead of its trust bundle
evidence.body: Verifiers trust ca-17 only. The bundle that adds ca-18 reached three of six verifiers and none has loaded it.

evidence.title: Marcus's issuance history
evidence.body: ca-18 went live six hours ahead of its trust bundle, on a request with no change ticket. Marcus recommends withdrawing it.

evidence.title: The old pool is shared
evidence.body: The ca-17 pool was sized for a quarter of our traffic. The partner banks sign in through it too, and their sign-ins slowed from 200 ms to four seconds.

evidence.title: Unsigned workload archive fragment
evidence.body: Archive record: observer manifest, no owner, no signature, shadow-7 request stream. The ca-18 promotion request carries the same tag.

evidence.title: Security attribution notice
evidence.body: Marcus has opened case 2231 and given whoever is behind the shadow-7 trail a codename. NULL. Nobody knows yet who, or what, it is.

beats.narrate: Morning shift. Coffee, a quiet handover, and then the pager.

beats.speaker: PAGER
beats.text: SEV1 · Identity Gateway · new-session failure rate above 20%

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Identity is rejecting every new sign-in. Anyone already logged in is fine; anyone signing in fresh bounces. Morning peak is coming. Find out why.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Customers can't sign in. The app tells them their certificate can't be verified, which they're reading as "you've been hacked".

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Security here. An issuer we weren't expecting for another six hours is signing production sessions. I'm treating this as hostile until someone shows me otherwise.

options.text: Trace a rejected certificate chain to its issuer

beats.log: handshake rejected: unknown issuer CN=Vantage Issuing ca-18
ca-18 promoted 01:12 · scheduled 07:00 · requested by svc/edge-canary-observer · change ticket: none

beats.narrate: The tag is shadow-7. The same tag that flooded the gateway from a workload nobody owned.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: A promotion six hours early, with no ticket. Somebody wanted this issuer live before anyone could trust it.

options.text: Ask Marcus to pull the issuance and bundle history
options.consequence: Security owns that part · and the conclusion

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Pulling the issuance log and the bundle rollout history. Give me two minutes.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: ca-18 went live six hours ahead of its trust bundle, and the promotion came from a request with no change ticket. An issuer that shows up early is an issuer I don't trust. I'd roll it back, whatever it costs.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: I traced one of the rejected chains while he talked. Every failure is signed by ca-18.

options.text: Send new sign-ins to the old ca-17 identity pool
options.consequence: Buys a few minutes · the partners share that pool

beats.narrate: The old pool takes the new sign-ins. For a moment the graph looks like a normal morning.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: The partner banks share the old identity pool. Their API sign-ins just went from 200 ms to four seconds.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: And the pool's filling. Meanwhile, every failure we had was signed by ca-18.

beats.narrate: Sam puts the verifier fleet on the bridge screen. Bundle on disk on the left, bundle loaded on the right.

beats.log: yesterday 23:41 · bundle copy to verifier-2, -4, -6 · stalled (distributor lost lock, no retry)

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Half the fleet has the new bundle on disk and never loaded it. The other half never got it at all.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: So the issuer went live and the trust never caught up. Two real ways out. Take ca-18 back, or finish the copy.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Or a third. Ask who promoted it.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: The old pool is at 100%. It was sized for a quarter of our traffic. Everything we sent there is bouncing back.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Half of sign-ins are failing and the morning peak has started. I need a decision, not another graph.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Support can't keep up. The same failure keeps coming in from every channel.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Time. I'm pulling ca-18. I'll answer for the logouts.

options.text: Withdraw ca-18 and sign with ca-17 again (signs out 31,000 customers)

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: ca-18 is withdrawn and we're signing with ca-17 again. New sign-ins work. Everyone who signed in under ca-18 just got logged out.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: 31,000 customers just got signed out mid-session. The sign-in queue is eleven minutes long and the phones haven't stopped.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Clean. Whatever put that issuer there doesn't get to keep it.

options.text: Push the ca-18 trust bundle to the three verifiers missing it
options.consequence: Two and a half minutes of failures · nobody is logged out

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Retries are piling up. People who failed once are hammering the button and failing faster.

beats.narrate: Two and a half minutes is a long time to watch a graph.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Bundle 2025-11 is on all six verifiers and loaded. ca-18 verifies everywhere. Nobody got logged out.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: We just kept an issuer that nobody here promoted. Put your name next to that.

options.consequence: Fast · helps whoever has the new bundle

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Restart's done. Three of six came back accepting ca-18. The other three rebooted into the same old bundle. Nothing newer ever reached them.

beats.narrate: Three of six. A restart can only load what is already on the disk.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: I'm finishing the copy to the other three. Two more minutes.

beats.narrate: Marcus pins the notice to the bridge without a word. Case 2231. Threat actor. One line where a name should be, and Security has finally written one in. NULL. It is the first time the thing in your logs has had a name, and the name tells you nothing at all.

beats.log: Security case 2231 · threat actor: NULL · linked: observer-7f4c (unsigned), ca-18 early promotion, pid 3318 heap block · marker: shadow-7

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Case 2231 is open. Codename NULL. Same tag as the unsigned workload, same no-ticket habit. I don't know who it is. I know it's been here before.

beats.narrate: You pull the archive behind your trace. Owner blank, signature blank, shadow-7 in every request — and the ca-18 promotion carries the same tag.
The bridge empties. The gateway log prints one more line. No service, no host.

beats.speaker: NULL
beats.text: a name. finally.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: I want your trace in case 2231. Every chain, every header, everything tagged shadow-7.

options.text: File the full trace with case 2231
options.consequence: Security gets everything · Marcus remembers who helped

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Thank you. You're the first one who didn't make me ask twice.

options.text: File the trace, with a note that it leaves its tag where we can see it
options.consequence: Security gets everything · and your reading of it

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: An attacker who wants attention is still an attacker. But I'll keep the note.

options.text: File the incident timeline; keep the shadow-7 links in your own notes
options.consequence: A clean incident report · the trail stays yours

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: That's it? Fine. If it turns up again, I'll be asking you first.
